title: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables and Quadratic Equations
shortDescription: Solving by substitution/elimination, consistency conditions, discriminant and root relations.
genZNote: Two lines either meet once, never, or are the same line. A quadratic's discriminant tells you the plot twist before you solve.

sections.heading: Pair of Linear Equations
bullets: Forms: a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂.
Unique solution if a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂; no solution if a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂; infinitely many if all three ratios equal.
Methods: substitution, elimination, cross-multiplication x = (b₁c₂ − b₂c₁)/(a₁b₂ − a₂b₁).
Example: 2x + 3y = 12 and x − y = 1 → x = 3, y = 2.

sections.heading: Quadratic Equations
bullets: ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0); roots = [−b ± √(b² − 4ac)]/2a; D = b² − 4ac.
D > 0 two distinct real roots; D = 0 equal roots; D < 0 no real roots.
Sum of roots = −b/a; product = c/a. Equation with roots α, β: x² − (α + β)x + αβ = 0.
Word problems: speed/time, areas, consecutive numbers lead to quadratics — reject negative lengths or time.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Linear pairs are classified by coefficient ratios; quadratics by the discriminant and root relations.

commonTraps: Do not accept negative values for physical quantities.

sources.name: Standard quantitative aptitude reference (R.S. Aggarwal, Quantitative Aptitude)
